note: Casefold's transaction typologies: fixed rules over the traced transfers that label wallets and transfers in the graph ((:Address)-[:SHOWS]->(:TxTypology), SENT.typologies). A label is a lead for review, never proof. params are the thresholds the rules use; guidance links each typology to the source that names the pattern.

typologies.name: Transfer with a listed party
typologies.rule: Sender or receiver is a wallet the sanctions lists give for a listed party.

typologies.name: Sanctioned instrument
typologies.rule: The transfer is in an instrument that is itself under a transaction ban (for example A7A5 in the EU since 25 November 2025).

typologies.name: High-risk counterparty
typologies.rule: Sender or receiver carries a label in a high-risk category (scam, mixer, darknet, ransomware, fraud).

typologies.name: Exchange or service
typologies.rule: Sender or receiver carries the label of an exchange or other service: a deposit to or withdrawal from a provider.

typologies.name: Fan-out (distribution)
typologies.rule: A wallet sends one asset to at least {min} different wallets within {hours} hours.

typologies.name: Fan-in (aggregation)
typologies.rule: A wallet receives one asset from at least {min} different wallets within {hours} hours.

typologies.name: Pass-through (rapid in and out)
typologies.rule: Within {hours} hours of receiving an amount, a wallet sends on at least {ratio} of it in the same asset.

typologies.name: Structuring below a threshold
typologies.rule: At least {count} stablecoin transfers between the same two wallets within {days} days, each between {band} and 100% of a threshold ({thresholds}); USD stablecoins compared with EUR thresholds one to one, as an approximation.

typologies.name: Peeling chain
typologies.rule: Bitcoin: at least {hops} transactions in a row where a wallet sends most ({share} or more) on to one new wallet and a small part elsewhere.

typologies.name: Asset change (swap)
typologies.rule: A wallet receives one asset and sends another within {days} days (for example USDT in, ETH out).

typologies.name: Round trip
typologies.rule: Money in one asset returns to the wallet it left within {hops} hops.

typologies.name: Large stablecoin transfer
typologies.rule: One stablecoin transfer of at least {usd} (USDT, USDC).

typologies.name: Lookalike or spam tokens received
typologies.rule: A wallet receives tokens that imitate a known asset or carry advertising in their name (address poisoning, scam tokens); at least {min} such transfers.

typologies.name: Address poisoning
typologies.rule: A wallet receives dust or a fake token from an address that copies a real counterparty of it: the same first {prefix} and last {suffix} characters, or the same last {long_suffix} (after the fixed 0x/T/bc1 start). Dust is at most {dust}. Money later sent to the lookalike means the poisoning may have worked.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
guidance.says: Transfers split into small amounts or kept below reporting thresholds.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
guidance.says: Virtual assets deposited and withdrawn again at once, without further activity.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
guidance.says: Virtual assets sent on at once to several wallets or providers, especially in places with little relation to the customer.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators related to transaction patterns
guidance.says: Many small amounts collected from unrelated wallets, then moved on or cashed out.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions; transaction patterns
guidance.says: Conversion between virtual assets, at a loss or with extra fees, without a business rationale.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators related to anonymity; source of funds or wealth
guidance.says: Funds to or from mixers, darknet markets, ransomware, fraud or theft addresses.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators in the source of funds or wealth
guidance.says: Transactions with addresses linked to sanctions or other illicit activity.
Screen counterparties and beneficiaries of incoming and outgoing crypto transfers; act on a hit.
Screening covers the transaction, not only the client; blockchain analysis before and after the transfer.

guidance.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
guidance.says: Several high-value transfers in a short period, or staggered and then inactive.
Information on originator and beneficiary must accompany crypto-asset transfers between providers; missing information must be detected and handled.
Transfers to or from providers not authorised in the EU, decentralised platforms or self-hosted addresses are risk factors.
The report does not name peeling chains; its closest example is a chain of automated transfers across many wallets and exchanges.
